title: Military Occupational Specialties MOS 155A--Fixed Wing Aviator (Aircraft Nonspecific); 155E--C-12 Pilot, 155F--Jet Aircraft Pilot and 155G--O-5A/EO-5B/RC-7 Pilot.
raw_text:
8-155. Military Occupational Specialties
MOS 155A--Fixed Wing Aviator (Aircraft Nonspecific); 155E--C-12 Pilot, 155F--Jet Aircraft
Pilot and 155G--O-5A/EO-5B/RC-7 Pilot.
    a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
    b. Prerequisite. DA Cir 601 Series.
    c. MOS 155A, 155E, 155F, and 155G are non-accession MOS. All MOSs at the WO1 and
CW2 level in AOCs 152, 153 or 154 are feeder MOS for 155A, 155E, 155F, and 155G. MOS
155E, 155F and 155G may be substituted for MOS 155A CW5 positions at all levels.
    d. Associated SQI
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) B--Aviation Safety Officer.
         (4) C--Instructor Pilot.
         (5) F--Senior Instructor Pilot and Instrument Flight Examiner.
         (6) G--Aviation Maintenance Officer.
         (7) H--Standardization Instructor Pilot.
         (8) I--Tactical Operations Officer.
         (9) J--Engineering Test Pilot.
         (10) L--Maintenance Test Flight Evaluator.
         (11) P--Parachutist.
         (12) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (13) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI (Refer to table 6-6 for (list of universal ASI’s associated with this MOS)).
         (1) 5A--Joint Air tactical Operations Officer.
         (2) 5U--Air Operations Officer.
         (3) B2--UH-60 Pilot.
         (4) D8 – Government Flight Representative (GFR)
         (5) E1--UC-35 Pilot (for use with MOS 155A and 155F only).
         (6) E7--C-23 Pilot.
         (7) E8--C-26 Pilot.
         (8) E9--FCA-XX Pilot.
        (9) F3--RC-12D/G/H Pilot.
        (10) F4--RC-12K/N Pilot.
        (11) F5--O-5A/EO-5B/RC-7 Pilot (not for use with MOS 155G).
        (12) F6 –MC-12 Pilot (for use with MOS 155A and 155E only).
        (13) G2--Instructor Pilot (not for use with positions coded with SQI C).
        (14) G7--Aviation Related (authorized for grades CW3 and above).
        (15) G8--Aviation Safety Officer (not for use with positions coded with SQI B).
        (16) H2--Aviation Life Support Equipment Officer.
        (17) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (for use with MOS 155E, 155F and
155G (Effective 202410).
   f. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial awarding of MOS 155AEFG.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
               (b) Meet medical qualifications. WO1 and CW2 must--
                     1. Initially meet the medical examination requirements of Class I medical
standards as prescribed by AR 40-501.
                     (a) A physical demand Rating of Moderate (GOLD)
                     (b) A physical profile of 111121
                     (c) Color discrimination of red/green
                     (d) Correctable distant vision acuity 20/50 near vision acuity Correctable 20/20
in each eye
                     (e) Qualifying Scores
                      (1) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ)-0120cm, Seated Power Throw
(PT)-0350cm, Strength Deadlift (SD)-0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR)-0036 shuttles in
Physical Demand Category in “Moderate’ (Gold).
                      (2) 40 or above on selection Instrument for Flight Test (SIFT)
               2. Class II medical standards must be maintained once an officer is on flight status.
               (c) Maintain height and weight standards per AR 600-9 and AR 40-501.
               (d) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Technical Certification Course (IERW
for AOC MOS152 through 155).
               (e) Successfully complete the appropriate aircraft qualification training.
               (f) Be commissioned upon promotion to CW2.
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(1) above.
               (b) Successfully complete the Aviation Warrant Officer Advanced Course
(AVWOAC).
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(1) above unless awarded ASI G7 through
board action.
               (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(3) above unless awarded ASI G7 through
board action.
               (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Plans flights, ascertains factors such as load, weight, fuel supply, route, altitudes
or schedules as necessary to safely accomplish mission.
               (b) Supervises loading and unloading of aircraft to ensure load stability, balance and
adherence to aircraft load limitations.
               (c) Pilots and commands assigned aircraft under tactical and nontactical conditions
for military purposes.
               (d) Conducts pre/post-administrative and tactical mission briefings.
               (e) Performs aeromedical evacuation missions.
               (f) Performs aerial evasive maneuvers.
               (g) Maintains Aircrew Training Program requirements in appropriate aircraft.
               (h) Detects satisfactory and unsatisfactory aircraft system or flight performance.
               (i) Executes emergency operating procedures for assigned aircraft.
               (j) Performs electronic surveillance and intelligence gathering missions.
         (2) CW3 performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(a) through (i) above.
         (3) CW4 performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(a) above.
         (4) CW5--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(a) above.
               (b) Provides guidance, advice and counsel to commanders and other staff members.
    h. Grading and position titles. The following grades are used to code positions into one of four
definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals
CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:
         (1) Table 8-155A-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (2) Table 8-155A-2. Standards of grade TDA.
         (3) Table 8-155E-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (4) Table 8-155E-2. Standards of grade TDA.
         (5) Table 8-155F-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (6) Table 8-155F-2. Standards of grade TDA.
         (7) Table 8-155G-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (8) Table 8-155G-2. Standards of grade TDA.
    i. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following table:
          (1) Table 8-155AEFG. Physical requirements.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
